comments_text: Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals that this sequence is most similar (37.04%) to NA-CATH. K: 31%; F=R: 14%; G: 12%. Activity: active against E. coli (MIC 12.5 uM), B. subtilis (MIC 0.8 uM), A. baumannii clinical strain (MIC 6.3 uM), Enterobacter spp. (MIC >25 uM), K-pneumoniae DSM 30104 (MIC>25 uM), P. aeruginosa DSM 1117 (MIC 9.4 uM), S. aureus DSM 11729 MRSA (MIC 12.5 uM), E. faecium (MIC 1.6 uM), Y. pestis EV76 (MIC 12.5 uM), B. anthracis Sterne (MIC 12.5 uM), and S-pneumoniae D39 (MIC > 25 uM). In vitro Toxicity: Human RBC: HC50>250 uM, not hemo.lytic. Resistance development:no:bacteria:E. coli: E. coli did not develop resistance to the peptide after 21 passages. comments_text: Discovery: it is another form isolated from the same bacteria strain. This form differs from the previously isolated peptide (AP00635) only at the C-terminus, with one extra W. It is unclear whether this is a different form or the previous one results from protease degradation. Hence, it is treated as a different peptide at this stage. Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals that this sequence is most similar (97.3%) to Mesentericin Y105. Activity: active against L.mesenteroides Y 105 (MIC 263 uM), L. ivanovii 496 (MIC 34 nM), L. paramesenteroides 19 (MIC 38 nM), L. curvatus DSM 20 019 (MIC 708 nM), L. sake DSM 20 017 (MIC 37 nM), C. divergens DSM 20 623 (MIC 538 nM), and C. piscicola DSM 20 730 (MIC 742 nM). SAR: this 37-residue form, with W37, is 10,000-fold more active than the 36-residue peptide originally isolated. Structure: no structure in aqueous solution but became helical in 50% TFE.
title: Covalent structure, synthesis, and structure-function studies of mesentericin Y 105(37), a defensive peptide from gram-positive bacteria Leuconostoc mesenteroides
